categories.description: Choose the matching syntax and comparison rules.
categories.name: Matching

options.detail: Matching is case-sensitive by default. Some Unicode letters have special case relationships, so matching can depend on the locale.
Use | for alternatives and parentheses for grouping without backslashes. Quote the pattern so the shell passes these characters to grep.
Dots, stars and brackets match themselves. A fixed string can match part of a line.
At each end of the match, grep requires the edge of the line or a character other than a letter, digit or underscore. For instance, cat matches in cat-food but not in cat_food.
With several patterns, a match for any one of them excludes the line.

options.detail: Use -e to pass a pattern beginning with a dash. Newlines within its argument separate patterns, and -f can supply additional patterns from a file.

categories.description: Choose the information printed for matches.
categories.name: Output

options.detail: Numbering begins at 1 in each input file.
Several matches on one line count once. With -v, the count covers lines matching none of the patterns.

options.summary: List files with a selected line
options.detail: Print each qualifying file name once and stop reading that file at its first selected line. With -v, a file qualifies if any line matches no pattern.
Empty matches produce no output. With -z, each printed match ends with a null byte. Context options have no effect with -o.
The default group separator is a line containing two dashes (--). With -o, grep omits context lines.
options.summary: Show lines before and after each selected line

variants.meaning: Context lines on each side of a match

forms.grammar: Nonnegative base-10 integer, without unit suffix. Zero adds no context. Counts apply separately before and after each match; overlapping groups are merged. Overflow saturates at the implementation's intmax_t maximum instead of imposing a smaller guessed fixed limit.

special_values.meaning: Do not add surrounding context lines

when_absent.meaning: Add no surrounding context through this option.
